weekly: NOTE: Readings will be no more than 15-20 pages: The pre-democratic polis: Possible readings include: Aeschylus’ Eumenides, Herodotus’ Persian Council, Thucydides’ Archaeology and/or Periclean, Funeral Oration
The Government in Crisis: Possible readings include: Thucydides’ Mytilenean and/or Melian Debates, Lysias, Against Eratosthenes; Plato’s Apology
The State in Crisis: Possible readings include: Aristophanes, Women of the Assembly/Lysistrata/Birds; Thucydides’ Corcyraean stasis and corresponding analysis of war, Xenophon, Constitution of Sparta
Alexander: Possible readings include: Plutarch’s Alexander, Arrian's Anabasis
Alexander and the Hellenistic Kingdoms: Selected secondary reading as well as artwork and inscriptions
Between Myth and Truth-The Origins of Rome: Possible readings include: Livy (Romulus, Numa, Superbus), Dionysius of Halicarnassus
The Roman Republic: Possible readings include: 12 Tablets, Polybius Book 6
The Problems of the Republic: Possible readings include: Cicero, Against Verres 2; On the Command of Pompey
The Problems of the Republic: Possible readings include: Cicero, Against Verres 2; On the Command of Pompey
Civil War: Possible readings include: Sallust, On the Catilinarian Conspiracy
The death of the Republic: Possible readings include: Suetonius, Augustus. Field trip to the Res Gestae in Ankara
The Epic Empire and the Pax Augusta: Possible readings include: Vergil, Aeneid 1, 6
Empire in Verse: Possible readings include: Ovid, Horace, Martial; Lucan, Pharsalia
Imperialism and its discontents: Possible readings include: Tacitus, Agricola, Germania, Annals
